thread:
morgan: quick sync — we need one surface for 'continuation handshake' across py/ts/go. we keep drifting between opaque tokens and richer objects
priya: agreed. main constraints: ergonomic for py/ts, zero-copy for go, and clear retry semantics
jonas: can we enumerate options and tradeoffs?
liam: option A: single opaque continuation token (string). pros: simple, language-agnostic, easy to store. cons: hard to do partial resume, debugging is meh
priya: option B: structured cursor object with helpers (e.g., {stream_id, offset, checksum}) exposed in SDK as first-class. pros: introspection, nicer retry rules. cons: surface complexity, versioning pain
morgan: option C: stream-id + client-side window manager (SDK keeps light state, server returns minimal resume handle). idea: SDK exposes resume() and pause(), no token plumbing for app devs
jonas: runtime/transport impact? how does this map onto unary vs streaming gRPC/WS/HTTP2?
liam: for streaming transports, we can piggyback KV cache positions, so resume is mostly server-side. unary/paged endpoints need explicit continuation handle in request body
priya: language ergonomics: python wants an iterator that hides resume. ts wants both iterator and explicit token. go wants explicit small struct to avoid allocations
morgan: what about idempotency & retries? if we return an opaque token that encodes a sequence id + checksum, consumers can safely retry until token advances
jonas: but encoding sequence into token leaks implementation and prevents future server-side refactor. we could version tokens (v1: base64 json, v2: opaque).
liam: proposal: default SDK surfaces per-lang:
- python: lazy iterator with opt-out param resume_token=True -> yields (item, resume_token) if caller wants it
- ts: async iterable + explicit token API (getToken()/resumeFrom(token))
- go: return small ResumeHandle struct and ResumeFrom(handle) functions
priya: prototype snippet for python:
```py
for chunk, token in client.stream_messages(resume_tokens=True):
    process(chunk)
    save(token)
# or simple: for chunk in client.stream_messages():
#               process(chunk)
```
liam: ts sketch:
```ts
const it = client.streamMessages();
for await (const chunk of it) { /* opaque by default */ }
// or
const { token } = await client.getResumeState();
client.resumeFrom(token)
```
morgan: storage & rotation: tokens should be short-lived (hours) by default for privacy. longer retention via opt-in policy header for enterprise
jonas: telemetry: SDK should surface token -> map to server trace-id for debugging. avoid leaking PII in tokens
priya: backwards compat: token format must encode version. server supports old formats and can emit migration warning in header
liam: open question: should SDK do automatic resume on transient transport errors? my vote: yes for streaming by default, with toggle. for unary pages, don't auto-resume without caller consent
morgan: +1. make auto-resume opt-out flag in ctor: autoResume=true by default for iterables
sre-bot: deploy note: this will touch the runtime handshake; coordination with eng-runtime required. please file a small migration checklist before rollout
priya: next steps: i can draft a concrete interface PR for python + TS, liam can do go stubs. aim for API review next week
morgan: perfect. assign owners and we can lock on token versioning scheme in the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
